37 The charge carriers in a metal wire are free electrons.
Which statement about the charge of each free electron is correct?
A
The magnitude of the charge increases with the potential difference across the wire.
B
The magnitude of the charge is zero unless there is a potential difference across the wire.
C
The sign and magnitude of the charge do not depend on the potential difference across the
wire.
D
The sign of the charge depends on the potential difference across the wire.

hints: Focus on the wording charge of each free electron, not the current or drift speed in the metal wire.
Recall that electron charge is a fixed elementary charge of magnitude $1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ with negative sign.
Ask yourself what the potential difference across the wire actually changes - the force and drift motion of electrons - and whether that can change what an electron is.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the property of one free electron in the metal, while potential difference is applied across the whole wire.
State the physics rule: every electron has the same intrinsic charge $q = -e = -1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, where the minus shows negative sign and $e$ shows magnitude.
Explain the role of potential difference: it provides an electric field that exerts a force $F = qE$ and produces a drift velocity and current $I = nAvq$.
Check the cause-and-effect: changing potential difference changes $E$, drift velocity and $I$, but it does not create charge or alter $e$.
Therefore sign and magnitude are unchanged by potential difference. This is option C.

A.explanation: The electron charge magnitude is fixed at $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and is not increased by a larger potential difference.

B.explanation: Each electron carries its negative charge whether or not there is a current; potential difference causes drift, not the existence of charge.

C.explanation: Charge is an intrinsic property of the electron, so both its negative sign and magnitude $-e$ are independent of the potential difference.

D.explanation: Reversing the potential difference reverses the direction of drift velocity and current, but electrons remain negatively charged.
